title: Commonwealth Entities (Payment Surcharges) (Consequential Provisions and Other Matters) Bill 2024
short_title: Commonwealth Entities (Payment Surcharges) (Consequential Provisions and Other Matters) Bill 2024

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would make the consequential and transitional changes that sit alongside the Commonwealth Entities (Payment Surcharges) Bill 2024, which gives Commonwealth entities express authority to charge payment surcharges.
It would apply the new surcharging authority retrospectively to payment surcharges charged or collected on or after 1 January 2003, when the Reserve Bank of Australia first regulated surcharging.

Its consequential amendments and retrospective provisions would commence with the Payment Surcharges Bill, while its tax liability provisions would commence only once the Tax (Imposition) Bill also commences.
changes: Schedule 1 would repeal existing provisions in other Commonwealth laws that authorise surcharges on particular payments, along with legislative instruments made under them, for future payments only.
Schedule 2 to the Administrative Decisions (Judicial Review) Act 1977 would be amended so that decisions to impose or refund a surcharge are excluded from the right to request a statement of reasons.
A person the Commonwealth would otherwise owe money to because a surcharge was charged on a non-surchargeable payment would be liable for payment surcharge tax, set off against that amount.
The retrospective provisions would have no effect to the extent they would result in an acquisition of property otherwise than on just terms.
summary.affected: Commonwealth entities that charge payment surcharges, people who have paid surcharges to them since 1 January 2003 and people seeking reasons for surcharge decisions are affected.
